questions.q: Which earlier chapter's toolkit -- state pull, state list, state rm, and import -- did Lesson 31's recovery actually use?
options: Chapter 7, Terraform in CI/CD
Chapter 6, Bicep Deep Dive
Chapter 3, State Management
Chapter 1, Terraform Fundamentals
questions.explain: Those four commands are Chapter 3's state management toolkit, applied here to a real incident instead of a clean textbook example.

questions.q: Why did Lesson 30 use directory-per-environment state instead of Terraform workspaces?
options: Because of the reasoned tradeoff from Chapter 5 (Lesson 18): isolating blast radius and approval requirements between dev and prod
Because .tfvars files require a separate root folder by definition
Because Terraform workspaces cannot be used with the azurerm provider
Because the module itself only supports being called once
questions.explain: Lesson 18's tradeoff, from Chapter 5, is the direct reason Caldwell Ridge isolated dev's and prod's state rather than sharing one workspace backend.

questions.q: What role did Chapter 7 (Terraform in CI/CD) play in this capstone, even though no single lesson's code shows a pipeline?
options: It's the layer -- plan on pull request, an approval gate, drift detection -- that should catch a Lesson 31-style incident before it reaches a confusing production error
It replaced the need for a remote backend entirely
Chapter 7 played no role in this capstone at all
It is only relevant to Bicep deployments, not Terraform ones
questions.explain: The capstone's network module is exactly the kind of configuration a CI/CD pipeline from Chapter 7 is meant to protect, catching drift before it becomes an incident.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real job this capstone proved, beyond simply writing working HCL once?
options: Writing HCL so it survives being reused across environments, re-run safely, and repaired after a real incident
Memorizing every Terraform resource type that exists for Azure
Choosing Bicep over Terraform for every future project
Avoiding modules entirely in favor of one large configuration file
questions.explain: The capstone's real lesson is durability -- a module and state setup that holds up under reuse, re-runs, and a genuine production incident.
